root_cause: The existing Janitor identifies recurrent slow jobs, but does not attribute their duration to independently repeated completed provider job steps; agents could optimize unrelated stages based on a one-off peak.

observed_evidence.sample: 28 executed jobs / 13 attempts / longest 353000ms / p95 wait 3000ms; single-window diagnostic, no speedup proof

failed_approaches: Infer step bottleneck from slowest job alone
Count parallel matrix jobs as distinct attempts
fix: Derive bounded completed-step-phase evidence entirely from existing GitHub job-list rows plus canonical executed-job IDs, attempts, SHAs and runtime. Require >=20 executed jobs, >=5 attempts and >=3 independent attempts per exact workflow ID/job/step group. Reject invalid/mismatched steps and return at most five step median/max hypotheses without release or automatic action.
prevention_rule: Never count skipped/cancelled/zero/negative/outside-job steps, spoofed name, duplicate number or unverified job. Reuse existing canonical Janitor/Brain owner and source snapshot, no extra scheduler, API read, gate bypass, paid capacity or unverified speedup. Step attribution does not prove critical path.

invariants: only use existing Janitor GitHub job response
20 executed jobs / 5 distinct run attempts minimum
exact SHA, workflow ID, job and step identity
no fabricated causal critical path or speed improvement
safe with missing, duplicate, invalid or malicious provider steps

terminal_rule: Only call source released after exact-head Required and CodeQL, protected auto-merge, exact-main proof and existing Janitor runtime step evidence; keep #4661 open for repeatable optimization benchmark.
